reporting-org.narrative: DEPARTMENT FOR SCIENCE, INNOVATION AND TECHNOLOGY

title.narrative: : Implementation of photovoltaics through an innovative mini-grid expansion model for rural African & Asian communities - (IMPHORAA

description.narrative:
The IMPHORAA project focuses to the speed market penetration of a combined set of proven technologies (off-nano-grids, PV, cooling, water pumping) to be successfully deployed primarily in the Philippines and amplified in Madagascar markets where they are eagerly needed by rural off-grid communities.
Nanoe (NAN) has already installed PV nanogrids in Madagascar that cover the needs of 2500 final users (household and commercial units) and 15000 beneficiaries (people enjoying the benefits). This technology is now further developed with cooling and water pumping capabilities which has the capability of widening the business model, while reducing chemical battery need, in order to optimise the successful "lateral electrification" model. This approach has been decided as the ideal pathway to lead electrification in the Philippines too. Frequent catastrophic events make the need for decentralised electrification and fast maintenance capabilities urgent and this is possibly the only way to allow the rural areas reach their development goals and put an end to poverty and total lack of opportunities. This approach not only improves the livelihood of people in these areas, but also aims to significantly reduce poverty by paving the road for sustainable agriculture and micro-entrepreneurship.
The proposed IMPHORAA approach tackles the energy trilemma as it implements three trends, which are impacting the global energy sector at an unprecedented pace: decarbonization, digitization, and decentralization.
The IMPHORAA team has a diverse profile and this we believe makes the consortium ideal to carry out a sensitive, ambitious and quite detailed electrification model that ensures affordable pricing, secure access to quality power and 70% less need for chemical storage, thanks to use of cooling storage as a means to balancing the intermittent solar power production.
